title: Migrate to your own database
content:
## When & why to migrate

By default, every deployed Emergent app stores its data in a **managed MongoDB database** provided by the platform. This database is included in your subscription at no additional cost and scales automatically to handle typical workloads.

<Info>
Database migration is only available for **deployed** apps. Apps in development always use the Emergent-managed database.
</Info>

You may want to migrate to your own external MongoDB database when:

- **You need advanced control** over backups, retention policies, or access patterns
- **You're approaching production scale** and want dedicated resources or performance SLAs
- **You have compliance requirements** that mandate a specific cloud region or provider
- **You want to consolidate data** across multiple services in your own infrastructure
- **You plan to take your app outside Emergent** and want full ownership of the database layer

<Callout type="tip" title="Data ownership">
Your data is always yours, even on the managed database. See [Your data & ownership](/your-data-ownership) for details on exports and portability.
</Callout>

Most apps run successfully on the Emergent-managed database indefinitely. Migration is optional and typically reserved for apps with specific infrastructure or compliance needs.

## The migration process

Migrating to your own database is designed to be **zero-downtime**. Your app continues to serve traffic while data is copied in the background.

<Steps>
<Step title="Provision your MongoDB database">
Set up a MongoDB instance with your preferred provider (MongoDB Atlas, AWS DocumentDB, self-hosted, etc.). Ensure it's accessible from the internet or configured with the appropriate network rules.

You'll need a **connection string** in the standard MongoDB format:

```
mongodb+srv://username:password@cluster.provider.net/database_name
```
</Step>

<Step title="Add the DATABASE_URL environment variable">
In your app's deployment settings, add a new environment variable:

- **Key**: `DATABASE_URL`
- **Value**: Your MongoDB connection string

The platform automatically detects this variable and triggers the migration process.
</Step>

<Step title="Background migration begins">
Emergent starts copying data from the managed database to your external database. This happens in the background without interrupting your app.

- **Writes continue to the Emergent database** during migration
- **Reads are served from the Emergent database** until migration completes
- Migration time depends on data volume (typically minutes to hours)
</Step>

<Step title="Cutover and synchronization">
Once the initial copy is complete, Emergent synchronizes any writes that occurred during migration, then switches your app to use the new database.

- **The app restarts automatically** to connect to the new database
- **Cold start time may be slightly longer** on first request ([learn more](/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting))
- The managed database is retained for 7 days as a rollback option
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
Ensure your external database has sufficient resources and connection limits for your app's workload. The Emergent-managed database automatically scales; your own database does not.
</Warning>

### Rolling back

If you encounter issues after migration, you can roll back by removing the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable. Emergent will restore service using the managed database (available for 7 days post-migration).

<Note>
Any writes to your external database after cutover **will not** be reflected if you roll back. If possible, test the migration on a staging or development copy first.
</Note>

### After migration

Once your app is running on your external database:

- **You are responsible for backups, monitoring, and scaling**
- Emergent continues to deploy, build, and serve your app normally
- The managed database is permanently deleted after the 7-day retention window

For more on how data is handled in Emergent, see [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) and [Your data & ownership](/your-data-ownership).
